[{"sha":"7eed8aacae3b3e62b3d2c927d5ed2c21e6e12396","node_id":"C_kwDOGKvm49oAKDdlZWQ4YWFjYWUzYjNlNjJiM2QyYzkyN2Q1ZWQyYzIxZTZlMTIzOTY","commit":{"author":{"name":"vercel-gh-bot-3[bot]","email":"282332853+vercel-gh-bot-3[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","date":"2026-10-30T16:35:18Z"},"committer":{"name":"GitHub","email":"noreply@github.com","date":"2026-10-30T16:35:18Z"},"message":"perf: Speed up prefix environment matching (#14867)

## Change
Extend the existing non-Windows literal environment-matching fast path
to lists containing literals and single trailing-prefix wildcards, such
as `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`. Avoid regex compilation for these common framework
patterns while preserving unresolved inclusions/exclusions, escaped bang
markers, Unicode, and the regex rule that a wildcard suffix cannot
contain LF. Complex patterns and Windows retain the existing regex
implementation.

Hypothesis: eliminating regex construction for common framework
environment patterns reduces task-hashing overhead and improves short
CLI workflows. Existing wildcard memoization still limits this saving to
distinct pattern lists, not every task.

Author model: `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`.
Reviewer model: `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5`
(`fable_performance_reviewer`).

## Methodology
Built and preserved baseline and candidate independently with identical
default features and `cargo build --profile release-turborepo -p turbo`.
Linux x86_64, 8-vCPU Intel Xeon 2.90 GHz guest, 16 GiB RAM; Rust nightly
2026-07-03, Zig 0.17.0, Hyperfine 1.20.0. No concurrent builds during
timing; CPU power mode unavailable.

Directly invoked each preserved binary with `run build --dry=json
--daemon=false --cwd=<repository>`, telemetry/update notifications
disabled, stdout discarded. Warm filesystem; no task execution or
task-cache reset. Workloads were selected before measurement:

- Turborepo `9330903fb870682d5c3239d2acac597fd4fb29e8`: 103 packages /
51 tasks.
- create-t3-turbo `8f945b7bb3bfb3ca8358d48b1ff0214079bc11ee`: 13
packages / 13 tasks.
- Payload `24ac89558c7d778b6dc563f0ed82178d4b1c58bb`: 52 packages / 52
tasks.

Primary confirmatory protocol: 12 blocks per repository, three warmups
per binary per block, then 20 baseline/candidate pairs per block. Each
block contains ten AB and ten BA pairs, shuffled with seed `20260804 +
block`; each pair uses `hyperfine --warmup 0 --runs 1 --export-json
<file> <first-command> <second-command>`. This gives 240 measured
samples per binary per repository. Bootstrap 100,000 resamples of block
median speedups, rather than treating serial samples as independent.
Retained every sample, including outliers.

Also retained eight earlier grouped AB/BA blocks (three warmups, 20
measured samples per binary per block), plus clean-checkout baseline and
same-command serial after batches. The later interleaving addresses
order asymmetry observed in the grouped batches.

## Evidence and limitations
For create-t3-turbo:

| Interleaved measurements | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Descriptive pooled median | 21.542 ms | 20.781 ms |
| IQR | 2.273 ms | 2.264 ms |

Mean paired-block median saving: **0.728 ms**. Mean block speedup:
**3.32%**, 95% block-bootstrap CI **1.95–4.82%**. Eleven of twelve
blocks improve; both command orders improve. Earlier grouped blocks
independently show 4.83% [2.83–6.79%].

The unpaired serial t3 baseline/last-after medians are unfavorable
(22.72 → 24.07 ms); these sessions drift over time and are not the
causal timing evidence. All were retained and reviewed. No timing
improvement is claimed for the local checkout (inconclusive) or Payload
(order-sensitive), and no build-time, scaling, Windows, cold-filesystem,
or memory claim is made. Local interleaved blocks 5–8 ran after a
transport-session checkout reset; the exact patch was restored and the
final four blocks plus final correctness checks were repeated. External
corpus revisions and both preserved binaries remained unchanged.

A separate Divan 0.1.21 benchmark corroborates the mechanism: matching
`NEXT_PUBLIC_*` against 130 variables drops from approximately 46 µs to
0.51–0.66 µs across four balanced blocks. Comparable Chrome traces show
lower task-hashing/precompute spans, but contain waits and unrelated
variability; neither instrumented timings nor the microbenchmark
substitute for the end-to-end evidence.

The release binary grows by 2,048 bytes (50,359,440 → 50,361,488). Long
lists of prefix patterns scan the environment once per prefix and were
not separately benchmarked.

## Review
The opposite-model reviewer received the complete diff, exact commands,
environment/corpus identities, diagnostics, final validation results,
and all 2,640 wall-time samples inline. It independently recomputed the
statistics and approved the exact final diff with **no blocking
findings**, limited to common-prefix matching and the measured t3
dry-run workflow.

Non-routine semantic verification compared both binaries' task hashes,
environment summaries, framework selections, and input maps across all
three workloads with representative framework variables set; all
compared outputs matched.
